page.layout: Running head and page number at the top; below them two engraved coin medallions with their legends; below those one column of running text in two paragraphs.

main_text.p: BALDVINVS secundus, Roberti Constantinopolitani Imperatoris prædicti, filius, post patrē Imperator creatur anno mundi 5188. à Christo nato 1226. sed cùm per ætatem haud esset idoneus, Ioannes Brennius Ierosolymitanus quidem nomine solum Rex, Italia euocatus, adiutor ei datur: cuius filiam in uxorem duxit, spreta quæ illi offerebatur Regis Pontici filia: unde bellum atrox obortū. Balduinus multis bellis exhaustus, ac pressus filium, & crucis dominicæ partem Venetis oppignerat, templorum omnium donaria aufert, exercitum ingentem ad Bosphori fauces obiicit: interim Byzantium proditione amittit: profugus cū patriarcha, naui in Euboeam delatus est: ita dum externam vim timet, à domestica opprimitur, anno imperij 33. tunc Græci imperium recipiunt Costantino-politanum, quod Franci annos 58. tenuerant. Vide Blon. lib.7. deca.2. Egna.lib.2. Volater.lib.23. Aem.lib.7. Cosm.Mun.lib.4.

MICHAEL Palæologus pulso Balduino, Byzantium capit, imperat quo anno mundi 5221. à Christo nato 1259. Hic Ioanni Lascari tutor datus à patre Theodoro moriente, puerum interemit: imperium sibi ac suis destinans, primum Achaiæ regno Guillelmum spoliat, Genuensium classe fretus: deinde Balduini opes frangit, urbem (ut dixi) capit. Bellum cum Venetis diu gessit, quem facile imperio deturbassent, nisi Genuenses obstitissent. induciis factis Lugdunum ad concilium quod Gregorius decimus indixerat, venit: faciléque illi cum Pontifice convenit: unde tantam suæ gentis invidiam contraxit, ut mortuo sepultura negarint. mansit tamen imperium in familia eius annis 193. donec in Turcarum manus devenit, Mahomete, ui capto Byzantio, Constantinum obtruncante, anno mundi 5414. à Christo nato 1452. Vide ut supra. regnat an.34.

page.notes: The two medallions are engraved portraits (Baldwin II on the left, Michael Palaeologus on the right); their legends are printed in the medallion rims and are transcribed above as printed fragments. Legend text on the left is partly cut off at the edge of the engraving. Printed "Costantino-" is hyphenated at the line end. Two word forms are doubtful: "ui capto" follows the u/v rule for a vowel. No marginal notes or catchword.
